QF.id: Cat III AIF Fees and Performance_23

question.text: If the High-Water Mark of an open-ended Cat III AIF is consistently rising, it signals:

answer.text: Poor fund performance and loss of investor trust
Superior past/present performance and a good indicator for future returns

explanation.text: The Logic: A rising HWM signals superior fund performance and is used by managers to showcase track record. The Trap: Static HWM signals poor performance; rising HWM is NOT a compliance or leverage indicator. Cross-Exam Context: Common hedge-fund marketing metric. Distributor's Pro-Tip: Cross-check the HWM trajectory with benchmark to distinguish true alpha from beta drift.
